purpose: first deterministic XZ profile for Blender/LiDAR implementation

core_mapping.mapping_rule: profile +X -> core +X; route +X chainage -> core +Y; route +Y left -> profile -X -> core -X; route +Z -> core +Z
core_mapping.note: The route-frame handedness and the selected profile-side convention are explicit integration choices; the production core axes are not changed.

civil_lining.shape: concentric circular shell for initial cross-section

extrados.basis: documented 5.5/5.1 family; concentric 0.20 m structural depth used for closed initial shell

coarse_ring_topology.warning: The 11-segment 5.5/5.1 arrangement is consistent with the documented DZMO family; the exact factory drawing set/segment CAD has not been located, so this remains a topology reference rather than series-accurate geometry.

blocked_fields: key central angle and exact wedge geometry
exact radial-rib count and angular positions per segment type
unambiguous factory/series designation for the 11-segment Figure 4.14 variant
underlying manufacturing drawing numbers referenced by TU 35-521-90 are not publicly available as dimensioned tubing drawings in the inspected source set

initial_geometry.reason: Stage 10.4 must replace the Stage-9 shell without inventing series-specific N/C/K central angles, ribs, bolt holes or rebates

running_rail_and_track.rail_profile_source: existing reference_impl R65 engineering reconstruction from GOST R 51685-2022

sleeper_top_z_m.reason: Fig.1.14 vertical 220 mm callout is used as UGR-to-sleeper/fastening support datum for the deterministic initial section.

fastening.family: KD-65 separate fastening on timber sleeper

initial_rail_seat_height_m.derivation: R65 base z (-0.180) - sleeper top z (-0.220) = 0.040 m support gap; subtract 0.006 m under-baseplate pad and 0.014 m rail-pad total thickness -> 0.020 m baseplate rail-seat height
initial_rail_seat_height_m.source_geometry_context: P10-ALBUM-KD65 drawing 96 provides the local KD65 plate profile including 16/20.5/23.6/55.6 mm callouts, but the exact metro assembly datum reconciliation is not separately dimensioned

rail_pad.reason: Use the 1995 KD65 drawing instead of the previous generic R65 pad envelope; Moscow-specific rubber formulation remains unconfirmed.

under_baseplate_pad.reason: Replaces the previous D65-family 360x170x8 fallback with the actual KD65 drawing.

track_screw.head: flat
track_screw.comparison_note: The general-railway KD65 album drawing 98 uses 24x170; the Moscow metro Fig.1.17 explicitly labels 24x150, therefore 24x150 is retained for this service preset.

initial_visual_head.reason: metro source fixes 24x150 and flat-head family but the exact head solid required by the production preview is not completely dimensioned in the selected metro figure

nut.quantity_basis: deterministic metro-figure interpretation; the 1995 general-railway KD65 Table 22 lists four M22x22 nuts, so quantity is service-variant dependent

visible_sleeper_after_concreting.rule: track-concrete surface terminates 0.010 m below sleeper top outside the fastening footprint

initial_clamp_geometry.reason: Frolov fixes assembly topology and M22x75 hardware; exact KDP-2 spring-clamp solid and local slot/axis coordinates are not required/resolved for the initial profile

gauge_definition.measurement: distance between inner working faces of running-rail heads
gauge_definition.implementation_note: Rail profile symmetry axes must be offset by the analytic R65 working-face half-width at this z level; do not place profile axes at +/- gauge/2.

central_drain.reason: Fig.1.14 dimensions the running-tunnel central drain at 900 mm clear width and 530 mm depth from UGR; adjacent text gives the general 0.5-0.6 m depth range. Exact corner radii/side finishing are not numerically stated.

water_release_groove.note: caption states 25x50 mm; initial orientation uses 50 mm width x 25 mm depth

initial_position.rule: represent the source-dimensioned 50 mm wide x 25 mm deep groove as a centered longitudinal notch in the 0.900 m central drain bottom for deterministic v1 geometry
initial_position.reason: Fig.1.14 dimensions the groove but the inspected source text does not provide a separate numeric lateral offset

shoulder_geometry.rule: outside sleepers, track-concrete top follows 0.03 transverse fall toward central drain; sides fill down to circular intrados; do not use Cmk as a physical surface
shoulder_geometry.nominal_surface_rule: adjacent to sleepers use sleeper-top minus 10 mm as the local datum and apply the 0.03 fall toward the central drain; exact hand-finished breakpoints remain replaceable

initial_surface_reference.reference_x: absolute timber sleeper end |x| = sleeper length / 2 = 1.325 m
initial_surface_reference.rule: set concrete top z=-0.230 m at the outer end of the 2.650 m timber sleeper (10 mm below the flat sleeper top), then apply 0.03 fall toward the central drain; continue the same plane outward until it intersects the physical 5.1 m intrados
initial_surface_reference.reason: Fig.1.14 gives approximately 10 mm sleeper exposure at the drawn sleeper edge and a 0.03 transverse fall; anchoring the fall at the sleeper end preserves that exposure instead of burying the sleeper ends

nominal_concrete_top_at_sleeper_datum_z_.derivation: sleeper top -0.220 m minus Fig.1.14 0.010 m exposure

derived_min_concrete_bottom_z_at_rail_on.derivation: sleeper bottom -0.385 m minus minimum 0.160 m track concrete under sleeper at rail position

walkway.type: raised concrete pedestrian/service walkway integrated with invert fill

top_clear_width_m.derivation: physical intrados intersection minus Fig.1.14 inner-edge offset; not derived from clearance envelope

walkway.service_era_interpretation: legacy raised banquette/walkway; not a modern retrofit-only element

initial_geometry.inner_riser_contact_rule: share x=+1.660 m boundary with Stage-10.2 track concrete; omit hidden lower contact span and retain exposed riser above concrete

placement.note: placement constraints only; object dimensions come from separate profile/assembly sources

rail_profile.era_warning: manufacturer 2021 profile is used as dimensional fallback for legacy Moscow silhouette; exact historical Moscow rolling section not proven identical

initial_mesh_profile.rule: use exact 90 mm base, 80 mm top, 20 mm web and 118 mm overall height; preserve the 46/40/23 mm vertical callout bands while linearizing undimensioned transition radii
initial_mesh_profile.warning: transition radii/curvature are not dimensioned in the catalog figure and are intentionally linearized

cover_profile.fallback_note: Only the historical clearances and support offsets are asserted for the legacy wooden box. The modern polymer profile is a silhouette fallback, not a historical extrusion.

effective_initial_geometry.derivation: historical 223 mm rail+protective vertical envelope minus 23 mm lower-edge offset fixes 200 mm effective cover height; modern silhouette contributes wall thickness/shape proportions only. Width is adjusted so the 134 mm base with 2 mm side walls gives 130 mm internal clearance, preserving at least 20 mm lateral clearance around the 90 mm maximum RK width

protective_assembly.historical_cover_family: legacy wooden-board protective box per 1986 VNiR installation terminology

support.shape_rule: arched channel-like tunnel bracket fixed to timber sleeper; reproduce topology from Frolov Fig.1.20

attachment_to_timber_sleeper.fasteners: three track screws in the conventional pre-composite support arrangement
attachment_to_timber_sleeper.adjustment_rule: legacy bracket position is adjusted at the sleeper; exact slot/hole coordinates are not required for initial profile

initial_geometry.reason: Frolov fixes curved-channel topology and sleeper attachment; TSN fixes 540x620x100 mm resource envelope, but exact bend radii and hole coordinates are unresolved

schedule.rule: generate an independent 5.0 m target chain, then snap each support to the nearest deterministic timber sleeper so the legacy three-screw sleeper attachment remains physical

service_era_preset.civil_era: classic postwar 5.5/5.1 cast-iron family; exact factory series unresolved
service_era_preset.service_reference_era: late Soviet / legacy configuration documented in 2001 textbook
service_era_preset.permanent_way: timber sleepers embedded in track concrete
service_era_preset.contact_rail: bottom-collection steel contact rail with late-Soviet/2001 legacy bracket-insulator suspension topology represented by Frolov Fig.1.20; legacy wooden protective-box constraints, with modern box silhouette fallback only
service_era_preset.walkway: raised +0.200 m banquette opposite contact rail
service_era_preset.cable_infrastructure: legacy open wall-mounted cable racks; geometry generated by separate equipment preset
service_era_preset.lighting: legacy tunnel luminaires; exact luminaire body not required for initial cross-section
service_era_preset.modernization_rule: civil lining and service preset are independently replaceable; modern LVT/LED/cables may be applied later without changing civil shell
service_era_preset.service_era_selection_basis: service configuration is fixed independently of civil lining/opening year; it is a documentary 2001-reference preset, not a statement about every surviving 5.5/5.1 tunnel today

first_version_exclusions: exact cable-rack and luminaire product geometry
